author: haiku
label: c2-nat-haiku-01
changes: Renamed the download mode field to download_state, removed the separate applying value, and made the catch-up phase downloading with pages_complete true (Q5, Q6, Q1).
Replaced download_catchup_since with next_cursor, and made the swap copy it into live_cursor (Q1).
Added change_seq to each item of the page endpoint, and wrote the apply rule for pages and catch-up so it depends on that field (Q2, Q3).
Made the Wi-Fi gate apply before every download request, including each catch-up batch, not only between pages (Q4).
Made incremental sync (step 7) not run while a download is in progress, and stated what that means for the cursor and last_incremental_at (Q5).
Made the resync path write its state in one transaction and clear the watermark, so a kill during resync is recoverable. The 410 from catch-up now goes to the same resync step (Q6).
Stated the first-install state, and that download_state is separate from whether a catalogue exists (Q7).
Defined the purge horizon H precisely, stated that since equal to H is safe, and said purging creates no change rows (Q8).

Merged the separate clean-up step into the swap and resync steps, and dropped the separate clean-up step. Renumbered the server purge step as step 12. Failure cases stay with each step, so no separate table repeats them.
Added short definitions for the platform APIs (NWPathMonitor, WorkManager, background URL session) to the terms.
Added the purge confirmation to open question 2.
Summary now says how the current system works, then gives the flow in three sentences.
Terms: added Cursor and removed the unused Attempt term. Kept the platform API definitions.
Steps renumbered into one main flow (1 to 8), with a Trigger, Data moved, Kept in and On failure line in each, so every step stands alone. Steps 9 to 11 are resume, retries and background work.
Step 1 names its three triggers, and step 8 hands off straight to step 1 (answers Q9).
Step 5 now states why catch-up from W is complete when pages read products mid-download (answers Q10).
Step 9 owns the Wi-Fi resume and includes failed_exhausted, which step 10 already relied on (answers Q11).
Step 10 says the attempt count is per request, kept in memory, survives a cellular pause, and restarts at 5 on a new trigger (answers Q11).
Step 6 is the swap for both the first download and a resync, with the rename committing in the same transaction as the cursor and state (answers Q12 and Q13).
Step 7 says last_incremental_at is not reset at the swap, so the next trigger runs at once when it is old (answers Q12).
Server purge behaviour moved into the endpoint section, so it is stated once, and the purge step was removed as a client step.
Added a short table of what the rep sees in each state (answers Q14).
Open questions: added id reuse to item 2, added item 8 (telling the rep) and item 9 (stale catalogue after a failed resync). The browse-during-first-download question is still undecided.

Kept every fact from the brief and the first version, including the 500 and 1,000 limits, the 15-minute gate, the 7-day window, the 2 s doubling and 5-attempt limit, Wi-Fi-only downloads, and the storage and asset notes.
Summary cut from two paragraphs plus a separate Core idea section to one summary; the watermark idea is now stated once, in step 4, instead of in three places.

Summary now states how the system works today (Postgres change_seq, 7-day tombstones, settings-only SQLite, no sync API) before the new design, as the skill requires for a change to an existing system.

Terms list now defines every name a newcomer would not know: change_seq, tombstone, purge horizon H, watermark W, cursor, keyset pagination, product_next, product_live, swap, sync_state, 410 resync_required, gzip, NWPathMonitor, WorkManager, background URL session. Also defines Postgres and the catalogue file (why it is separate from settings).
Renamed next_cursor and removed download_catchup_since; the catch-up cursor is next_cursor, copied into live_cursor at the swap (junior Q1).
Endpoint table: each product item now carries change_seq, so the apply rule has a value to compare (Q2). Added the N = H safety argument and the note that purging creates no change rows (Q8).

Wi-Fi rules moved into their own section, The Wi-Fi gate, which covers the watermark request, pages and catch-up batches. Catch-up is stated to need Wi-Fi, and incremental sync is stated to be ungated (Q4). Retries waiting for Wi-Fi and keeping their count are stated in the gate and in step 9 (Q11).
Step 1 lists its three triggers explicitly, with the resync and resume handoff (Q6, Q9). A kill before the step 1 transaction is covered: nothing changed, so W is fetched again.

Step 4 (catch-up) carries the apply rules once, with the delete-with-no-row case (Q3). The completeness argument is kept but shortened to one line per case (Q10). The product-id-never-reused assumption points to open questions.
Step 5 (swap) is the same for first install and resync, and says the app reads only the name product_live, with the SQLite open-read check left to the implementer (Q13).

Step 6 (incremental sync) states that it does not run while a download is in progress, and that last_incremental_at is not reset after a swap (Q5, Q12). Added: a failed run still counts toward the 15-minute gate. This is a new reading, flagged as open question 5.
Step 7 (resync) merged the old step 9 with the 410 path from step 5, so there is one resync path (Q6). It states that product_live keeps serving until the swap.

Step 9 (retries) merged the retry policy into one place and lists the retry triggers. Waits of 2, 4, 8, 16 s, the 30-second total and the 5-attempt limit are kept. Other 4xx handling stays an open question.
The rep table gained a row for first install with failed_exhausted (Q14), and the table cross-refers to open questions by topic.
All nine open questions are kept, reworded plainly. Steps refer to them by topic, not by number.

Removed repeated statements of the same rule across sections. Every stated number, limit, setting and rule from the first version was checked and kept: 400,000 products, about 2 KB, 500-item pages, 1,000-item batches, 15 minutes, 7-day tombstone window, 2/4/8/16 s waits, 5 attempts, gzip, about 1 MB pages, one-at-a-time requests, Android and iOS Wi-Fi checks, and the rep-visible states.
